query: Let `R` be a commutative semiring. Equip `ArithmeticFunction R` with the topology of pointwise convergence (the discrete topology on each coefficient slot). Let `f : ι → ArithmeticFunction R` be a family such that for every `n`, `(f i) n = (1 : ArithmeticFunction R) n` for all but finitely many `i`. Then for every `n`, the partial products `∏ i ∈ s, f i` evaluated at `n` are eventually equal to `(eulerProduct f) n` as `s : Finset ι` grows along `atTop`.

    14  /-!
    15  # Construction of L-functions
    16  
    17  This file constructs L-functions as formal Dirichlet series.
    18  
    19  ## Main definitions
    20  
    21  * `ArithmeticFunction.ofPowerSeries q f`: L-function `f(q⁻ˢ)` obtained from a power series `f(T)`.
    22  * `ArithmeticFunction.eulerProduct f`: the Euler product of a family `f i` of Dirichlet series.
    23  
    24  ## Implementation notes
    25  
    26  We take the following route from polynomials to L-functions:
    27  * Starting from a polynomial in `T`, `PowerSeries.invOfUnit` gives the reciporical power series.
    28  * `ofPowerSeries` gives the local Euler factor as a formal Dirichlet series on powers of `q`.
    29  * `eulerProduct` gives the L-function as the formal product of these local Euler factors.
    30  * `LSeries` gives the L-function as an analytic function on the right half-plane of convergence.
    31  
    32  For example, the Riemann zeta function `ζ(s)` corresponds to taking `1 - T` at each prime `p`.
    33  
    34  For context, here is a diagram of the possible routes from polynomials to L-functions:
    35  ```
    36                     T=q⁻ˢ                     s ∈ ℂ
    37  [polynomials in T] ----> [polynomials in q⁻ˢ] ----> [analytic function in s]
    38            |                           |                           |
    39            | (reciprocal)              | (reciprocal)              | (reciprocal)
    40            v         T=q⁻ˢ             V          s ∈ ℂ            V
"}]
